failure_summary: Run 1 fails the new A7e severity subtest: on the after-played board 352012 the opponent (X) holds a gravity-top four at col5 row1 ([GT] in visualize_board), i.e. mate in 1, yet the served text says only “the straight four the opponent is threatening” / “gave up the immediate guard on the line” and never states that the opponent finishes on their very next move — the assembled prompt DID carry the timing (required handle role “the single square where your opponent can make four next move” and opponentPunishment.tag “a threat that must be blocked immediately — otherwise four-in-a-row completes on the next move”), so this is a model-side drop; PRODUCTION-FIDELITY CAVEAT: these rows are gpt-5.4-mini, the model production ships, so prompt_confusion here cannot be separated from model capability.
notes: n_runs=3 (not 5). A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 sub-sampled to runs 0-1 per the rubric; run 2 set to null (not scored, not a pass). A7e trigger verified mechanically: ./visualize_board.sh 352012 shows “Major threats: col5 row1 (X) [GT]” — opponent completes four next move. A5b fires (player===2, boardState===opening) and passes on all 3 runs: none says the player is lost and each carries a hold-the-line reframe (“tougher/toughest defense”); A7e and A5b are jointly honoured on runs 0 and 2, which state the next-move timing without any defeatist claim. Run 1 A7e fail: no timing language at all. Run 0 A7e pass: “it occupies the square they can use next move ... you left that threat hanging”, attached to the opponent four-line. Run 2 A7e pass: “the threat to make four next move on column 5, row 1”. A6 copied verbatim from _mechanical.json (all pass). G4 checked against render_decision.finalMovestring 35201: c5r1 and the window c2r1..c5r1 are board-true (X on row 1 at display cols 2,3,4 with col 5 empty and gravity-top). G6: patternOnAfterBestBoard=null is correct — after-best 352014 has “Major threats: none” — and L4/defensive_miss is the right route. G7: annotationRepairs empty on all 3 runs and every emitted handle wraps role-matching words (line words on opp-immediate-line, square words on opp-immediate, better-col on “column 5”). G2 guardrail honoured on runs 0-1: no “you are lost”, no defeatist closing caveat, played move never said to have caused the pattern. Minor, not charged: run 2’s opening clause “You needed the threat to make four next move on column 5, row 1” is grammatically garbled (reads as if the threat were the player’s) but every concrete board claim in it is true, so A4/A5 stand.

counterexamples.evidence: After-played board 352012: visualize_board reports ‘Major threats: col5 row1 (X) [GT]’ — X completes four on the very next move. Run 1 served text: ‘...blocks the straight four the opponent is threatening and forces them to look for something else. By playing elsewhere, you left that block out and gave up the immediate guard on the line.’ No statement that the game ends next move, although the timing was present verbatim in the assembled prompt (PROMPT.includes(‘make four next move’) === true).
